rows.title: Equal-distribution pair discrepancy bound
rows.record_statement:
Let $D({\bf p},{\bf q})$ denote the discrepancy between the color distributions of the matching left-right pair when the left and right shoes have distributions ${\bf p}$ and ${\bf q}$. In the equal-distribution case, write $D({\bf p},{\bf p})$. **Equal-distribution discrepancy bound.** One should have

$$
\sup_{\bf p}D({\bf p},{\bf p})<1.
$$

This is the analogue of the universal discrepancy bound under the constraint that the two shoe distributions agree. The paper describes it as plausible and leaves it open.
rows.source: Richard Arratia and Stephen DeSalvo, “On the Random Sampling of Pairs, with Pedestrian examples”, arXiv:1211.6486 (2013).
rows.what_was_proved: For every discrete probability law p on a countable colour set, the total variation distance between the common colour of two independent p-draws conditioned to match and the first chronological opposite-side matching colour in independent strictly alternating left/right arrivals is at most 255/256. The supremum over such laws is therefore strictly less than one.

rows.title: The bunkbed conjecture for transitive tournaments
rows.record_statement:
Let $T_n$ be the transitive tournament on $n$ vertices, and let $\operatorname{BBC}(E_7,T_n)$ denote the bunkbed conjecture in the $E_7$ model for $T_n$.

**The bunkbed conjecture for transitive tournaments.** The statement

$$
\operatorname{BBC}(E_7,T_n)
$$

holds for $T_n$.

The conjecture concerns whether the bunkbed inequality remains valid in the $E_7$ directed-graph model for this acyclic family. The supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.
rows.source: Lawrence Hollom, “The bunkbed conjecture is not robust to generalisation”, arXiv:2406.01790 (2024).
rows.what_was_proved: For every n and all vertices u,v of the transitive tournament Tₙ, the probability that (u,0) reaches (v,1) is at most the probability that it reaches (v,0) in the E₇ bunkbed. Reachability permits zero-length paths, and the n² independent fair bits give one token per horizontal arc per layer and one shared bidirectional vertical token per vertex.

rows.title: The asymptotic threshold conjecture for complete bipartite graphs
rows.record_statement:
Let $K_{2,l}$ be the complete bipartite graph with parts of sizes $2$ and $l$, and let $\tau(K_{2,l})$ denote its list color function threshold.

**Asymptotic threshold conjecture.**

$$
\tau(K_{2,l}) = \Theta(\sqrt{l}) \quad\text{as } l \rightarrow \infty.
$$

The preceding theorem proves a lower bound of order $\sqrt{l}$, while the conjecture asserts a matching upper bound and hence determines the asymptotic growth rate of the threshold.
rows.source: Hemanshu Kaul, Akash Kumar, Jeffrey A. Mudrock, Patrick Rewers, Paul Shin and Khue To, “On the List Color Function Threshold”, arXiv:2202.03431 (2023).
rows.what_was_proved: tau(K_{2,l}) = Theta(sqrt l) as l -> infinity, where tau(G) is the least k >= chi(G) with P_l(G,m) = P(G,m) for all m >= k; explicitly tau(K_{2,l}) <= max(4, ceil(1 + sqrt(2l))), matching the source's Omega(sqrt l) lower bound.

rows.title: Local weak convergence of random fullerenes to the planar hexagonal lattice
rows.record_statement: Let $F_n$ be a random **fullerene**, meaning a finite, connected, 3-regular planar graph with faces of degrees both 5 and 6, chosen uniformly from the set of fullerenes with $n$ vertices. A sequence of finite random graphs converges **locally weakly** to a random rooted graph if the rooted balls around uniformly chosen vertices converge in distribution. Let $\mathcal{H}$ denote the planar hexagonal lattice. **Local weak convergence conjecture for random fullerenes.** The sequence $(F_n)$ converges locally weakly towards $\mathcal{H}$. This concerns the local geometry of uniformly random fullerenes in the large-size limit. The source states that the claim remains open; it is part of the broader study of local weak limits of random planar graphs.
rows.source: Artur Bille, Victor Buchstaber, Simon Coste, Satoshi Kuriki and Evgeny Spodarev, “Random eigenvalues of graphenes and the triangulation of plane”, arXiv:2306.01462 (2025).
rows.what_was_proved: Let F_n be uniform on isomorphism classes of fullerene graphs with n vertices (connected cubic planar graphs, every face a pentagon or hexagon), n ranging over the orders admitting a fullerene. Then F_n converges locally weakly (Benjamini-Schramm, rooted at a uniform vertex) to the hexagonal lattice.

rows.title: The Q-index extremal conjecture for $K_{t,s+1}$-free graphs
rows.record_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$, with adjacency matrix $A$ and diagonal degree matrix $D$. Its signless Laplacian is $Q(G)=A+D$, and its $Q$-index $q(G)$ is the largest eigenvalue of $Q(G)$. A graph is **$K_{t,s+1}$-free** if it contains no subgraph isomorphic to the complete bipartite graph $K_{t,s+1}$. Let $s\geq t-1\geq1$, and let $n$ be sufficiently large. **The Q-index extremal conjecture.** If $G$ is a $K_{t,s+1}$-free graph of order $n$, then

$$
q(G)\leq\frac{n}{2}+s+t-2+\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\left(n-2+2s\right)^2-8s\left(n-2\right)+4\left(t-1\right)\left(n-t+1\right)}.
$$

Equality holds if and only if $G$ is the join of $K_{t-1}$ and an $s$-regular graph of order $n-t+1$. The conjecture is proposed as a spectral counterpart to extremal problems for $K_{s,t}$-free graphs; the authors state that they expect Problem C to be resolved completely in the next few years, but the asserted bound and equality characterization remain unproved here.
rows.source: Maria Aguieiras A. de Freitas, Vladimir Nikiforov and Laura Patuzzi, “Maxima of the Q-index: graphs with no K_s,t”, arXiv:1507.00625 (2015).
rows.what_was_proved: For integers s >= t-1 >= 1 there is N(s,t) such that every K_{t,s+1}-free graph G of order n >= N(s,t) satisfies q(G) <= n/2 + s + t - 2 + (1/2) sqrt((n-2+2s)^2 - 8s(n-2) + 4(t-1)(n-t+1)); among K_{t,s+1}-free graphs, equality holds exactly for joins of K_{t-1} with an s-regular graph of order n-t+1.

rows.title: Uniqueness of terminal transversals under $(213)\rightarrow(123)$ moves
rows.record_statement: Let $Y$ be the Young diagram under consideration, let $S_Y$ denote its transversals, and let $S_Y(213)$ denote the transversals avoiding the pattern $(213)$. For a transversal $T\in S_Y$, consider sequences of $(213)\rightarrow(123)$ moves, each replacing an occurrence of the pattern $(213)$ by $(123)$. **Uniqueness conjecture.** Starting with a transversal $T\in S_Y$, all sequences of $(213)\rightarrow(123)$ moves terminate in the same transversal $T'\in S_Y(213)$. This is a confluence assertion for the pattern moves and would make the $(213)$-avoiding terminal transversal canonically determined by the starting transversal. The supplied text does not indicate whether the assertion has been proved or remains open.
rows.source: Zvezdelina Stankova, “Shape-Wilf-ordering of permutations of length 3”, arXiv:math/0609644 (2006).
rows.what_was_proved: For every finite Young diagram with a transversal, rectangle-contained 213→123 swaps starting from that transversal have no infinite chain, and any two reachable transversals have a common descendant. There is exactly one reachable 213-avoiding transversal, attained by a finite maximal sequence, and every finite maximal sequence ends there.

rows.title: The local reversal edge conjecture for characteristic imset polytopes
rows.record_statement:
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a directed acyclic graph with skeleton $G$, and let $i$ be a vertex. Define $\mathcal{G}_{\downarrow i}$ by orienting every edge between $i$ and a neighbor toward $i$, while leaving all other edges as in $\mathcal{G}$. Write $c_\mathcal{G}$ and $c_{\mathcal{G}_{\downarrow i}}$ for their characteristic imsets, and let $\CIM_G$ denote the characteristic imset polytope associated with $G$. **Local reversal edge conjecture.** If $\mathcal{G}$ and $\mathcal{G}_{\downarrow i}$ are not Markov equivalent, then

$$
\operatorname{conv}\left(c_\mathcal{G},c_{\mathcal{G}_{\downarrow i}}\right)
$$

is an edge of $\CIM_G$. A linear bound on the diameter of $\CIM_G$ would follow from this conjecture; the source establishes quadratic bounds in general and linear bounds for trees and for the whole polytope, but does not resolve the conjecture for arbitrary skeletons.
rows.source: Petter Restadh, “Diameters of the Characteristic Imset Polytopes”, arXiv:2302.03647 (2023).
rows.what_was_proved: There is a five-vertex DAG C with eight arrows for which making vertex 4 a sink (one-based numbering) yields a DAG D on the same skeleton that is not Markov equivalent to C. The segment between their characteristic imsets is not an edge of the convex hull of characteristic imsets of all acyclic orientations of their skeleton; the certificate also shows it is not a face.

rows.title: Asymptotic dumbbell conjecture for the minimum sum-Balaban index
rows.record_statement:
Let $D_{a,b,a'}$ be a dumbbell graph on $n$ vertices, with clique sizes $a$ and $a'$ and connecting path size $b$, so that $a+b+a'=n$. Let

$$
c=\sqrt[4]{\sqrt 2\log\big(1+\sqrt 2\big)}.
$$

**Asymptotic dumbbell conjecture.** Among all dumbbell graphs $D_{a,b,a'}$ on $n$ vertices, the minimum is achieved for one with

$$
a=c\sqrt n+o(\sqrt n),\qquad a'=c\sqrt n+o(\sqrt n),\qquad b=n-o(n).
$$

This conjecture gives the predicted asymptotic shape of an optimal dumbbell graph: the two cliques have equal asymptotic size, while the path contains almost all vertices. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
rows.source: Martin Knor, Jaka Kranjc, Riste Škrekovski and Aleksandra Tepeh, “On the minimum value of sum-Balaban index”, arXiv:1701.02716 (2017).
rows.what_was_proved: Every eventually minimizing sequence of positive-integer dumbbell triples (a,b,a′) with a+b+a′=n and a≤a′ satisfies a/√n,a′/√n→(√2 log(1+√2))^(1/4) and b/n→1 as n→∞. The minimized objective is the sum-Balaban index of the graph formed by disjoint cliques and a disjoint b-vertex path, with every vertex of each clique attached to its respective path endpoint.

rows.title: Generalisation of the frustrated-triangle extremal conjecture to frustrated cycles
rows.record_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $\overline{G}$ denote its complement, and for $k\geq 3$ let $f_k(G)$ be the number of frustrated $k$-cycles, where a cyclic ordering $v_1v_2\dots v_k$ is frustrated when an odd number of its consecutive cycle edges belongs to $G$. For integers $t\geq 0$, let a $(t+1)$-star on $n$ vertices be the graph consisting of a star with $t+1$ leaves together with the remaining isolated vertices. **Frustrated-cycle generalisation conjecture.** For every $k\geq 3$, $t\geq 0$, and all sufficiently large $n$, if

$$
f_k(G)<f_k\big((t+1)\text{-star on }n\text{ vertices}\big),
$$

then either $G$ or $\overline{G}$ can be obtained from a complete bipartite graph by flipping at most $t$ edges or non-edges. This proposes an extension of the paper's structural result for frustrated triangles to frustrated cycles; its resolution is not given in the source.
rows.source: Teeradej Kittipassorn and Gabor Meszaros, “Frustrated Triangles”, arXiv:1411.1749 (2015).
rows.what_was_proved: For each integer k≥3 and t≥0 there is N(k,t)≥t+2 such that for all n≥N and all simple graphs G on n vertices, if the count of ambient injective unoriented k-cycles with an odd number of edges in G is strictly below that of the (t+1)-edge star plus isolates, then G or its whole complement differs from a complete bipartite graph in at most t unordered vertex pairs. Empty bipartition parts are allowed.

rows.title: The $d$-sequence conjecture for coefficients of uniform-matroid $Z$-polynomials
rows.record_statement:
For integers $m$ and $d$, and $0\leq i\leq d$, define

$$
b_m(d,i)=\sum_{h=0}^{m-1}\frac{i(h-m+1)+m}{(h+1)m}\binom{i-1+h}{h}\binom{d-i+h}{h}.
$$

A finite sequence of real numbers is an $n$-sequence when the associated polynomial has real zeros of one common sign. **The $d$-sequence conjecture.** The sequence $\{b_m(d,i)\}_{i=0}^{d}$ is a $d$-sequence for every $m$ and $d$. The conjecture is proposed as the analogue of the corresponding assertion for Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials and would support real-rootedness results for uniform-matroid $Z$-polynomials; its general status remains open.
rows.source: Alice L. L. Gao, Linyuan Lu, Matthew H. Y. Xie, Arthur L. B. Yang and Philip B. Zhang, “The Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials of uniform matroids”, arXiv:1806.10852 (2018).
rows.what_was_proved: For all positive integers m,d, coefficientwise multiplication by the displayed b_m(d,i), with binomials evaluated as real falling products divided by factorials, sends every real polynomial of degree at most d that is zero or splits over ℝ to zero or a polynomial that splits over ℝ. The binomially weighted symbol Σᵢ binom(d,i)b_m(d,i)xⁱ has degree d, constant coefficient 1 and strictly negative real zeros only.
